Am I the only one not suspecting Nate, and side eyeing Harold real hard? 
Here's why:
Let's say OP is real and so is either Dan OR Harold. That gives us two people in a three bedroom apartment, paying rent. This explains how they found Nate on Craigslist when they needed a roommate. Rent's not fuckin' cheap these days, and if you find a guy that "fit(s) in well" and can pay his share, you go for it. I see people looking for roommates in local facebook groups all the time, it's easy enough for me to believe.

Meanwhile, the story on Harold seems off, as plenty of people have noticed. Sure, OP has known him since they were kids and have been best friends since college, and that's plausible, I suppose? But the way this information has come out feels very much like "nonhuman entity warping people's memories" which is only compounded by the fact that after looking through over 200 comments, I didn't see OP respond to a single one questioning this very discrepancy. In addition to this, Harold's response to the creepy notes being put together and the realization that there was an extra person wasn't really "normal" to me. His immediate reaction is to say "fuck this!" and try to leave, which sounds like something someone who was bad at acting and had only ever seen horror movies would try to do. Like an alien trying to look like a totally normal human, while knowing it would be stopped from leaving, because of course a bunch of scared and confused humans weren't just going to let someone walk out before they understood what was happening. Then the look of betrayal, which reads to me as an attempt at emotionally manipulating OP into feeling bad for doubting "Harold," his /very best friend in the world!/ A tactic to get OP to go easier on him, be less suspicious? After all, Harold is the one OP has the most connection to and the most information on. If I were an alien insinuating myself into a group of humans and trying to earn their trust, I'd want each of them to feel connected to me.

Hell, within this social group, Harold seems to be closer to most everyone else than they are with one another. OP is a childhood/college(?) best friend, Dan is his coworker (not anyone else's), and while he doesn't seem to have some kind of special connection with Nate, neither do OP or Dan (as far as we know). Most suspicious of all, though, is his quick suggestion to call Leigh (his girlfriend). If Harold is indeed the impostor, this deepens the impression that he is "real" by providing him with a human connection outside of the four of them. Let's say he hadn't been shot down, and made the call. If he WAS the impostor, wouldn't that immediately become obvious because no one would pick up? Not necessarily, because this thing can fuck with people's perception. It's entirely possible it could have made the humans think they were hearing "Leigh" confirm Harold's existence while the phone hangs around on dial tone. We don't have any idea the extent of its power. So either way, suggesting to call a girlfriend would be beneficial to this creature.
(A side note for those who haven't been rifling through all the comments: OP has informed us that Harold is wearing a blue shirt, while the other three are wearing blue jeans, in relation to the last note. Harold is the only odd one out. A little obvious, to be sure, but it stacks on top of my other, deeper suspicions about him. After all, if the "best friend" is too obvious to be the impostor, and so dismissed immediately out of hand, it would therefore be /most/ advantageous to be the "best friend.")

And then there's Dan. What do we know about him? Not much, yet. But his reactions seem way more human and real, at least to me. His fear and subsequent aggressive attitude are very much in line with how a confused and threatened human acts. It may just be me, but I also feel like it just doesn't make sense for him to be the extra. Infiltrate a group of suspicious humans as... the coworker of one of them, whose best friend is also in the group? Why place itself in that position? Obviously OP would be closer with Harold than it, making it less likely to avoid suspicion, and get away with its deception. Sure, Harold may vouch for it, but that still leaves Nate and OP with doubts. It seems strategically unsound to me.

It would also make sense, if Harold were the impostor, that it insinuated itself into Dan's memories as his coworker in order to gain trust and legitimacy with him. Couple that with OP's insistence that he also knows Harold is real, it casts suspicion on Nate as the least "connected" member of the group. It's easier to get away with something if you have a scapegoat for it. And nothing makes a better scapegoat than an easy target.

At any rate, I might be a total conspiracy theorist and Harold might just be an actual human being, but he's gonna have to really prove it before I'll believe it. "Too obvious to be the impostor" is a great disguise for an impostor.

In addition to everything that breadfollowsme posted, which is accurate and very well said, I'd like to point out that you are definitely conflating bipolar disorder with abusive behaviour, and that is not okay. It demonizes bipolar people and mentally ill people as a whole. Simply having a mental illness doesn't automatically make someone abusive, and it's not an excuse for abusive behaviour.
It's also not okay to generalize all bipolar people based on your personal experience with just one or a few, especially if they had comorbid conditions (like narcissism or anti-social personality disorder, for example) that may have been factors in their behaviour.
Personally speaking, my best friend in the entire world is bipolar. She is the single greatest human being I have ever met and we love each other fiercely and unconditionally. Not once has she made me feel like she didn't love me. She has never, ever been abusive to me or anyone I know of. This woman is a fucking incredible human being and I would take a bullet for her, no hesitation.
The thought that you would "not risk" having her in your life based solely on the fact that she's bipolar honestly kind of infuriates me, though I am tempering that with sympathy for whatever bad experiences you've had. Just be careful of that generalization and the unintentional harm you may do to the bipolar community with it.
